In [[category theory]], a branch of mathematics, a '''stable ∞-category''' is an [[∞-category]] such that<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=Definition 1.1.1.9.}}</ref>
*(i) It has a [[zero object]].
*(ii) Every [[morphism]] in it admits a [[Glossary of infinity category|fiber]] and cofiber.
*(iii) A triangle in it is a [[fiber sequence]] if and only if it is a [[cofiber sequence]].

The [[homotopy category]] of a stable ∞-category is [[triangulated category|triangulated]].<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=Theorem 1.1.2.14.}}</ref> A stable ∞-category admits finite [[limit (category theory)|limit]]s and [[colimit]]s.<ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=Proposition 1.1.3.4.}}</ref>

Examples: the [[derived category]] of an [[abelian category]] and the ∞-category of [[spectrum (topology)|spectra]] are both stable.

A '''stabilization''' of an [[∞-category]] ''C'' having finite limits and base point is a functor from the stable ∞-category ''S'' to ''C''. It preserves limits. The objects in the image have the structure of infinite loop spaces; whence, the notion is a generalization of the corresponding notion ([[stabilization (topology)]]) in classical [[algebraic topology]].

By definition, the [[t-structure]] of a stable ∞-category is the t-structure of its homotopy category. Let ''C'' be a stable ∞-category with a t-structure. Then every filtered object <math>X(i), i \in \mathbb{Z}</math> in ''C'' gives rise to a [[spectral sequence]] <math>E^{p, q}_r</math>, which, under some conditions, converges to <math>\pi_{p+q} \operatorname{colim} X(i).</math><ref>{{harvnb|Lurie|loc=Construction 1.2.2.6.}}</ref> By the [[Dold–Kan correspondence]], this generalizes the construction of the [[spectral sequence]] associated to a filtered [[chain complex]] of [[abelian group]]s.
